stories.headline: US imposes fresh sanctions on M23 and FDLR leaders
stories.summary: The US Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control has imposed sanctions on senior leaders of the M23 rebel movement and the FDLR militia. John Imani Nzenze, M23 commander and chief of intelligence, and Gustave Kubwayo, FDLR commander and leader of an intelligence and special operations unit, are among those targeted. The sanctions are in response to alleged human rights abuses in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The move aims to escalate pressure on armed groups fueling conflict in the region. The sanctions will freeze any assets the individuals may have in the US and prohibit American citizens from doing business with them. The US action is part of international efforts to address the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, which has been plagued by violence and instability. The sanctions are intended to hold accountable those responsible for human rights abuses.

stories.headline: Uganda: Museveni Urges EU to Back Africa's Industrialisation As Uganda, Europe Mark 50 Years of Partnership
stories.summary: President Yoweri Museveni of Uganda has urged the European Union to support Africa's industrialisation and value-addition agenda. He argued that the continent cannot achieve meaningful prosperity while primarily exporting raw materials. Museveni made the call during a meeting with the European Union Ambassador to Uganda, Jan Sadek, at State House Entebbe, as they marked 50 years of partnership between Uganda and the EU. The President emphasized the need for Europe and other partners to pivot their engagement with Africa towards industrialization and value addition. He stated that exporting unprocessed raw materials has kept the continent poor decades after independence, and a shift in economic policy is necessary. Museveni welcomed the long-standing collaboration between Uganda and the EU, but used the platform to deliver a strong message on the need for economic transformation in Africa.

stories.headline: Somalia Says Al-Shabaab Bomb Commander Among 29 Killed in Operations
stories.summary: Somalia's National Intelligence and Security Agency (NISA) has killed 29 al-Shabaab militants, including the group's chief explosives operative, in operations in Middle Shabelle and Hiiraan regions. The operations, conducted with international support, targeted the town of Jabad Godane in southeastern Somalia. A senior Al-Shabaab commander, responsible for bomb operations, was among those killed. The Somali armed forces, in coordination with international partners, including the US Africa Command and the African Union, carried out the operations. The killings are part of an ongoing effort to combat al-Shabaab in Somalia, with the war against the group entering a critical phase. The international community has pledged support to Somalia in its fight against the militant group. The operations aim to weaken al-Shabaab's grip on the country and improve security in the region.

stories.headline: Africa’s Manufacturing Sector Grows, but Global Share Stays Small
stories.summary: Africa's manufacturing sector is growing, but its global share remains small. The continent accounts for less than 2% of global manufacturing output and 1.4% of manufacturing exports. Manufacturing value added as a share of Africa's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is below 10%. Despite growth, significant gaps remain, with manufacturing value-added per capita falling below pre-2014 levels. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is expected to drive a 28% surge in freight demand by 2030, but infrastructure investment is needed to support this growth. North Africa leads the continent's industrialization, but gains are slow and uneven. Africa's logistics performance also trails global benchmarks by 20-30%, hindering the sector's development. The continent's cotton market is estimated to grow from $6 billion in 2025 to $7.5 billion by 2030, indicating potential for expansion in specific industries.

stories.headline: iPhone 18, 18 Pro and Apple's first foldable: The biggest leaks revealed Leaks hint at iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and possible Fold in major 2026 refresh
stories.summary: Apple is expected to launch new iPhones in 2026, including the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, with a possible iPhone Fold. The iPhone 18 Pro lineup will feature 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch models, with slimmer bezels, flatter edges, and a more uniform matte rear panel. The devices may also have a smaller Dynamic Island. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to launch in September 2026, while the iPhone Fold's release date is uncertain. The standard iPhone 18 may be delayed until spring 2027. Leaks suggest Apple's first foldable iPhone will be part of a major refresh, with the company scheduled to introduce the foldable model alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September, according to sources.

stories.headline: Microsoft unveils first LLM, vibe coding model, and speech/text updates Microsoft has unveiled its first large language model called MAI-Thinking-1, which it says matches the performance of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6
stories.summary: Microsoft has unveiled its first large language model, MAI-Thinking-1, which matches the performance of Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6. The model has 35 billion active parameters and a 256,000-token context window, making it suitable for complex multi-step instructions, long-context reasoning, and code generation. Microsoft also announced MAI-Code-1-Flash, a model that generates source code for applications and websites based on written descriptions. Additionally, the company has introduced updates to its speech and text capabilities. MAI-Thinking-1 was preferred over Claude Opus 4.6 in blind side-by-side evaluations and matches its performance on coding tasks in SWE-Bench Pro, a software engineering benchmark. This move marks Microsoft's effort to build proprietary AI models and compete with other major players in the industry, including OpenAI and Anthropic.

stories.headline: ViewSonic Showcases AI-Enabled Learning and Integrated Visual Solutions Expansion TAIPEI, June 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ViewSonic Corp., a leading global provider of visual and EdTech solutions, is showcasing its expanding AI-enabled learning
stories.summary: ViewSonic Corp. is showcasing its expanding AI-enabled learning and integrated visual solutions at the ViewSonic Visual Solutions Forum 2026. The company, a leading global provider of visual and EdTech solutions, is featuring its latest AI-enabled ViewBoard interactive display. This technology offers enhanced capabilities for engaging and interactive learning experiences. As a provider of visual solutions for various spaces, including education, work, and entertainment, ViewSonic is highlighting its range of innovative monitors and projectors designed to enhance digital experiences. The company has retained its No. 1 position in the global interactive display market and continues to expand its offerings in AI-enabled learning and visual solutions, solidifying its position as a leader in the industry. The forum showcases ViewSonic's commitment to innovative and interactive technologies.

stories.headline: Nikon Metrology Receives Frost & Sullivan's 2026 Global Product Leadership Recognition for Excellence in Laser Radar BIW Inspection Recognized for advancing high-precision, in-line dimensional inspection and enabling data-driven manufacturing transformation in automotive production
stories.summary: Nikon Metrology has received Frost & Sullivan's 2026 Global Product Leadership Award for its excellence in laser radar BIW inspection. The company was recognized for advancing high-precision, in-line dimensional inspection, enabling data-driven manufacturing transformation in automotive production. In-line metrology helps reduce manufacturing costs by detecting deviations in real-time, allowing for immediate process corrections. This prevents defective part production, reduces rework needs, and shortens production cycles. The award acknowledges Nikon Metrology's innovation and growth excellence in reshaping the industry. The demand for metrology is increasing, particularly in semiconductor node scaling and advanced packaging, with growth in service-based and subscription models. Key players in the industry are driving this growth, with Frost & Sullivan recognizing companies that set high standards in competitive strategy, execution, and market responsiveness. Nikon Metrology's award showcases its leadership in the field of metrology.

stories.headline: Bafana World Cup visa bungle latest in long list of Safa snafus
stories.summary: Bafana Bafana's travel plans to the World Cup were delayed due to a visa application bungle by the South African Football Association (Safa). The team was initially grounded, but managed to depart on Monday after the issue was resolved. This incident is the latest in a series of mishaps by Safa. The team's delayed departure has raised concerns, with Minister Stephen McKenzie ordering a report on the matter. Safa's handling of the visa application process has been criticized, with the incident being seen as part of a larger pattern of errors by the organization. The delay has also sparked discussion about Safa's competence and ability to manage the national team's affairs. The team is now en route to the World Cup, but the visa bungle has left a negative impression.

stories.headline: Afghan women’s football team rises again after escaping the Taliban and years in exile
stories.summary: The Afghan women's football team is regrouping after escaping the Taliban and years in exile. Currently, 23 members of the Afghan Women United program are in a training camp in Auckland, New Zealand, where they will play games against a team from the Cook Islands. Despite the Afghanistan soccer federation not recognizing the women's team, FIFA has made a landmark decision allowing them to compete as Afghanistan's national team while living in exile. Team members, including Fatima Yousufi and Mona Amini, have found refuge after fleeing the Taliban. The team's resurgence is a significant development, enabling them to represent their country in international competitions despite the challenges they face. The training camp in New Zealand is a crucial step in their journey to rebuild and compete at the international level.

stories.headline: Ferrari extends multi-year F1 deal with Charles Leclerc
stories.summary: Ferrari has announced a multi-year contract extension with Charles Leclerc, securing his position as a driver for the team in the coming seasons. Leclerc joined Ferrari in 2019, after starting his F1 career with Sauber in 2018. The exact length of the contract was not specified, but the agreement ensures Leclerc will continue to drive for the Scuderia Ferrari team. This extension takes Leclerc off the Formula 1 market for the foreseeable future. The deal provides continuity for the Maranello-based team, with Leclerc set to remain a key part of their lineup. The announcement was made by Ferrari N.V. on June 3, 2026, confirming Leclerc's commitment to the team.

stories.headline: Done deal! Real Madrid to sign World Cup-bound right-back as Spanish giants trigger crazily low €20m release clause
stories.summary: Real Madrid will sign Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan after triggering his €20m release clause. The 27 is not correct he is 29-year-old defender will join the Spanish giants, providing competition for their current right-backs. According to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Dumfries has accepted personal terms with Real Madrid, and the deal is now effectively closed, with only formal steps remaining. The signing is expected to be completed soon, with Dumfries set to become Real Madrid's first major signing of the transfer window. Dumfries is currently bound for the World Cup, but his club future has now been secured with the Spanish giants. The €20m release clause has been described as "crazily low" given Dumfries' quality and experience.

stories.headline: 21, Mostly Foreigners, Killed In Massive Fire At Delhi Hotel
stories.summary: A massive fire at a hotel in New Delhi killed at least 21 people, mostly foreigners, on Wednesday morning. The fire started around 8:50 a.m. local time and tore through the building, prompting some to jump from the windows. Many of the victims were from Central Asia and Africa. Reports suggest the hotel had only one entry and exit door and lacked proper ventilation. Firefighters responded to the scene and rescued over 37 people, with 18 declared dead at the hospital. Officials are investigating the cause of the fire, which occurred in the Malviya Nagar area of south Delhi. The incident has been met with condolences from officials, including a statement from Mr. Gandhi expressing his deepest condolences to the bereaved families. The hotel fire is a significant tragedy, with many foreigners among the victims.

stories.headline: Annamalai quits BJP, to start new political ‘movement’
stories.summary: K. Annamalai, former Tamil Nadu BJP president, has quit the party to start a new political movement. Annamalai had been leading the BJP's campaign in Tamil Nadu for several years and was seen as a key figure in the state. He met with party national president Nitin Nabin and Union home minister Amit Shah in Delhi before making his decision public. According to sources, Annamalai plans to launch a volunteer-driven nationalist movement, likely under the banner of "Makkal Sakthi Iyakkam" (People's Power Movement), which could later evolve into a full-fledged regional political party. The move comes after Annamalai's reported dissatisfaction with the party's functioning in the state. He is expected to formally announce his new movement in the coming days, marking a significant development in Tamil Nadu's political landscape. Annamalai's decision is seen as a major setback for the BJP in the state.

stories.headline: 'No Constitutional Protection For Betting On Games Of Skill' : Supreme Court Upholds TN, Karnataka Laws Banning Online Games With Stakes
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of India has upheld the constitutional validity of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka laws that prohibit online betting and wagering on games, including those of skill. The court ruled that state legislatures have the competence to legislate on betting, even when the underlying game is one of skill. This means that while a game of skill may be constitutionally protected, betting or wagering on that game does not automatically enjoy the same protection. The laws in question ban online games played for money or stakes, including rummy, poker, and fantasy sports. The ruling gives states the power to prohibit such activities, allowing them to regulate online betting and wagering on skill-based games. The decision applies to games like rummy, poker, and fantasy sports, which are considered games of skill but can be played for stakes.

stories.headline: Kolkata's Surendranath College, a prestigious institution deeply intertwined with the freedom movement, has found itself engulfed in a massive controversy after
stories.summary: Kolkata's Surendranath College is embroiled in controversy after cash, liquor bottles, and a revolver were recovered from the premises. The incident has highlighted alleged misuse of power in Bengal educational institutions. Founded in 1884 by nationalist leader Surendranath Banerjee, the college is affiliated with the University of Calcutta and has a rich history intertwined with India's freedom movement. The college has previously faced financial issues, owing over Rs 50 lakh to the state finance department in 2003, prompting an inquiry by the Directorate of Public Instructions. The current controversy has brought the institution under scrutiny, raising concerns about the management and governance of educational institutions in the state. The recovery of a revolver and liquor bottles has sparked a massive outcry, prompting further investigation into the matter. The incident has tarnished the reputation of the prestigious institution.

stories.headline: Gold overtakes US treasuries as world's largest reserve asset by market value
stories.summary: Gold has surpassed US Treasuries as the world's largest reserve asset by market value, according to the European Central Bank (ECB). By the end of 2025, gold accounted for 27% of global central bank reserve assets, up from 20% a year earlier. In contrast, the share of US Treasuries fell to 22% from 25% over the same period. The shift reflects a 60% rally in gold prices and rising demand for the reserve asset. The ECB reported that gold's market value exceeded that of US Treasuries, marking a significant change in the composition of global official reserves. This development indicates a shift in central banks' preferences for reserve assets, with gold gaining prominence as a store of value and hedge against uncertainty. The data highlights the evolving landscape of global reserve assets.

stories.headline: Realpolitik, rare earths and India’s Myanmar calculus: The geopolitics behind Min Aung Hlaing’s Delhi visit
stories.summary: Myanmar junta chief and President Min Aung Hlaing visited India, sparking criticism from pro-democracy groups. The trip marked his first foreign visit as president since overthrowing a democratically elected government. India's decision to host him prioritizes strategic interests, including access to critical minerals and rare earths. During the visit, Indian Prime Minister Modi agreed to foster mineral and rare earth ties with Myanmar. The move has been met with anger from groups who accuse India of legitimizing the military regime. The visit highlights India's geopolitical calculus, balancing its desire for resources and regional influence with concerns over democratic values. Min Aung Hlaing's visit is seen as a significant development in India-Myanmar relations, with implications for the region's political and economic landscape. India's hosting of the junta leader has drawn international attention and criticism.

stories.headline: Four democracies, one ocean & a dragon in the room
stories.summary: Four democracies, India, the United States, Japan, and Australia, are forming an alliance in the Indo-Pacific region. This partnership is significant in the context of the region's geopolitics. The mention of a "dragon in the room" suggests China's presence and influence in the area. The alliance between these four democracies is seen as a response to the complex and high-stakes environment of the Indo-Pacific. The cooperation between India, the US, Japan, and Australia is expected to have implications for the region's security and stability. The formation of this alliance is a notable development in the ongoing dynamics of the Indo-Pacific, where multiple nations are vying for influence and power. The alliance aims to promote stability and cooperation in the region, amidst the presence of major powers like China.

stories.headline: Market volatility, MTF, geopolitics and investor mistakes: Jainam's CBO explains
stories.summary: Market volatility has increased due to escalating geopolitical tensions, contributing to a downfall in the market. The growing use of leveraged products and shifting investor behavior are also shaping conversations in India's financial markets. Geopolitics has taken center stage, changing the global market landscape over the past few years. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) has addressed questions about budgetary and economic outcomes, which may differ from their February 2026 projections. Additionally, the impact of the AI boom on stocks is being closely watched, with investors not expecting a third straight year of gains in 2025. Jainam's CBO has explained the factors contributing to market volatility, including market volatility, MTF, geopolitics, and investor mistakes. These factors are influencing investor decisions and market trends.

stories.headline: Sensex tumbles over 900 points, Nifty below 23,250. 6 key factors behind today's D-Street rout
stories.summary: The Sensex plummeted 930.67 points to 75,364.69, while the Nifty50 fell 345.65 points to 22,904.45, amid broad-based selling pressure across sectors. During intraday trade, the Sensex crashed over 1,150 points to 73,492, and the Nifty50 dropped to 23,151. The India VIX, measuring market volatility, jumped over 9% to 16.83. The Sensex had also traded below 73,750, down over 900 points or 1.2%, and the Nifty had slipped to 23,250, declining 250 points or 1.08%. The market decline was attributed to six key factors, leading to a sharp decline in Indian equity markets on Friday. The S&P BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 ended the day with significant losses, with the Sensex tumbling over 900 points and the Nifty slipping below the 23,900 mark.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty tank as US-Iran uncertainty, crude oil prices weigh on investor sentiment
stories.summary: Stock markets experienced a decline as uncertainty surrounding US-Iran relations and rising crude oil prices weighed on investor sentiment. The Sensex and Nifty indices tanked due to concerns over a potential disruption in oil and gas shipments. This comes after markets had previously hit record highs on reports of a possible ceasefire between the US and Iran, which could have reopened the Strait of Hormuz. However, recent developments have introduced new uncertainty, impacting investor confidence. The S&P 500 and Dow had closed modestly higher earlier in the week, driven by AI-related optimism, but were counterbalanced by US-Iran tensions. The current market volatility is being closely monitored, with investors seeking updates on the US-Iran agreement and its potential impact on global oil prices.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Crash Today: Sensex dips 930pts intraday; Nifty below 23,230; here's why
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant decline, with the Sensex dipping 930 points intraday and the Nifty falling below 23,230. As of 1:45 PM on Monday, October 7, the Sensex had fallen over 800 points to around 80,850, while the Nifty50 also declined. The market witnessed broad-based selling across various sectors, including IT, banking, and consumer durables. The Nifty IT index led the losses, with the Nifty 50 slipping below 23,600, a nearly 1% decline. The Sensex dropped over 850 points amid the selling pressure, impacting investor sentiment. The decline was part of a larger trend, with the Sensex and Nifty extending losses in afternoon trade on May 12, 2026, due to selling across major indices.

stories.headline: Nifty 50 tanks 250 points, Sensex crashes 900 points; why is Indian stock market falling today? Explained with 5 reasons
stories.summary: The Indian stock market has plummeted, with the Nifty 50 index tanking 250 points and the Sensex crashing 900 points. The decline is attributed to several factors, including renewed tensions in the US-Iran conflict and soaring crude oil prices. Additionally, global tech weakness and US interest-rate concerns have contributed to the sell-off. The Indian markets have also been impacted by IT stocks leading a broad sell-off. Other key factors behind the stock market decline include Trump tariffs and overall global economic uncertainty. The sharp decline has resulted in the Nifty sinking below 23,000, with experts citing a combination of domestic and global factors as the reason for the Indian stock market's downward trend. The sell-off has led to a significant loss of value in the Indian markets, with investors closely watching the situation.

stories.headline: Man linked to S$3 billion money laundering case admits to filing false tax information to IRAS
stories.summary: Wang Junjie, 43, has pleaded guilty to filing false tax information to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). He conspired with Su Haijin to submit false financial information about their company from 2020 to 2022. Wang, a corporate service provider, is linked to a S$3 billion money laundering case. He created and submitted fictitious invoices and transaction listings, and provided false information to obstruct the audit process. Wang's actions were part of a larger scheme to cheat IRAS. His guilty plea is related to the ongoing investigation into the money laundering case, which involves multiple individuals and companies. The case has been ongoing since 2020, with several individuals already implicated in the scheme. Wang's admission of guilt is a significant development in the investigation.

stories.headline: Node.js Moves to One Major Release Per Year, Starting with Node 27
stories.summary: Node.js is changing its release schedule to one major release per year, starting with version 27. The new release will be available in April 2026, and it will become a Long-Term Support (LTS) version in October 2026. This marks a shift from the previous twice-a-year major release cadence. All future releases will be LTS, eliminating the distinction between odd and even versions. An alpha channel will be available for early testing, with versioning following the semver prerelease format. This change aligns Node.js with the standard lifecycle of other major backend ecosystems, providing a more predictable and stable release cycle for developers. The move to a single annual release is intended to simplify the release process and provide more consistency for users. Node.js 27 will be the first release under this new strategy.

stories.headline: People are paying more for less cover, health insurance report shows
stories.summary: A recent health insurance report reveals that people are paying more for less coverage. Approximately one in four adults with Medicare give negative ratings to their monthly insurance payments and out-of-pocket prescription costs. The issue is exacerbated by rising premiums, with some ACA plans increasing by up to 59%. The biggest premium increases are affecting individuals with incomes above 400% of the federal poverty level, around $60,000. Additionally, Medicaid and ACA marketplace cuts are expected to leave roughly 15 million people uninsured by 2034. As a result, consumers are facing higher costs and reduced coverage, making it challenging to find affordable health insurance options. The cost of health insurance is expected to continue rising in 2026, affecting many individuals and families. Financial navigators are advising consumers on ways to navigate the changing landscape and find affordable coverage.

stories.headline: Sterling Infrastructure: Navigating Secular Data Center Tailwinds At A Premium Valuation
stories.summary: Sterling Infrastructure, a leading provider of infrastructure services, has earned a 'Buy' rating due to robust margin expansion, backlog growth, and secular data center tailwinds. The company's E-infrastructure segment leverages the AI and data center buildout, capitalizing on solid secular trends. Headquartered in Texas, Sterling Infrastructure operates across key US regions. Private equity firm Blackstone acquired the company for $10 billion in 2021 and has invested billions more to expand its data centers. The US data center market is substantial, with 4,313 listed facilities across 50 states. Sterling Infrastructure is well-positioned to benefit from the growing demand for data center services, driven by the increasing need for cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and data storage. The company's strategic expansion and investment in data centers are expected to drive growth and profitability.

stories.headline: Microsoft unveils AI models in push for independence from OpenAI
stories.summary: Microsoft unveiled its own cutting-edge artificial intelligence models in San Francisco, a step toward reducing dependence on OpenAI. At its Build developer conference, the company announced MAI-Code-1-Flash, its inaugural model in the AI coding space. This move marks a strategic push to decrease reliance on OpenAI technologies. Microsoft's primary goal is to develop in-house AI capabilities, showcasing a new generation of models. The announcement highlights the company's efforts to expand its AI offerings and reduce external dependencies. By developing its own AI models, Microsoft aims to enhance its position in the AI market and provide alternative solutions to its customers. The unveiling of these models demonstrates Microsoft's commitment to innovation and its desire to lead in the AI sector. This development is expected to impact the company's future AI-based products and services.

stories.headline: SpaceX plans to set IPO price at $135 per share, targeting record $75 billion raise, source says
stories.summary: SpaceX plans to set its initial public offering (IPO) price at $135 per share, aiming to raise a record $75 billion. The company, founded by Elon Musk, will sell 555.6 million shares, resulting in a valuation of $1.75 trillion. This would make SpaceX the seventh-biggest company in the world. The IPO is expected to be the largest in history, surpassing previous records. The fixed-price share sale is set to take place ahead of the company's investor roadshow. If successful, the IPO will provide SpaceX with significant funding to further develop its space exploration and technology initiatives. The planned IPO has been confirmed by sources familiar with the matter and reported by multiple news outlets.

stories.headline: SpaceX plans to price record-setting IPO at $135 per share, source says
stories.summary: SpaceX plans to price its initial public offering (IPO) at $135 per share, according to a source. The company aims to raise $75 billion by selling 556.6 million shares, which would be a record-breaking amount. The IPO is expected to take place on June 12, with a listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the prospectus, with Goldman Sachs as the lead left. SpaceX had accelerated its IPO timeline, initially planning to make its prospectus public by next week. The company's official IPO filing has been set up, paving the way for its public debut. If successful, the IPO would raise up to $80 billion, making it one of the largest in history. The exact timing and details of the IPO are subject to change, but June 12 is currently the targeted listing date.

stories.headline: SpaceX plans to raise $75 billion in IPO at $135 per share, source says
stories.summary: SpaceX plans to raise $75 billion in its initial public offering (IPO) by selling 555.6 million shares at a target price of $135 per share. According to sources familiar with the matter, Elon Musk's company will fix its IPO price ahead of its investor roadshow, rejecting traditional Wall Street conventions. The planned IPO price of $135 per share is expected to raise a record-setting $75 billion. The move comes as a surprise, with the company opting for a fixed price ahead of the marketing phase of the deal. The sources confirmed that SpaceX will offer 555.6 million shares at the target price, making it one of the largest IPOs in history. The IPO is expected to be a significant milestone for the private space exploration company.
